Honolulu, November 13th
'63
Dear Fand F (Family & Friends)
We took off for London at 9 a.m. on Oct. 30th. Our old friends
Chili Vaughn and 0. F. Studeman both former pilots who are now executives
came over to the Clipper lounge to see us off. Chili said that we would
fly South of hurricane Ginny and thus pick up a strong tail wind as hurri-
canes turn counter-clock wise.
Shortly after take off the Captain gave our estimated flight time
to London as 6:20, actually by my watch, take off to touch down was 6:19.
It is amazing how close the jets come to forecast or perhaps I should say
the forecasts to the jets.
Of course they climb up above the weather so
your flight is smooth all the way.
We stayed at a little hotel in London called the Goring on Ebury
Street near Buckingham Palace.
The hotel is more than 50 years old and
boasts of being the first hotel in the world to have a bath with every room,
the baths have changed very little in those fifty years. But the beds are
comfortable, the service perfect, the rates reasonable and the food delicious.
On the 31st we had lunch at the Cog d'or with our old friend
Jack Kelly, PAA Vice-President for Europe. That night we saw Lawrence of
Arabia - as Debby's father used to say of some sermons - it could be condensed.
Saturday, November 2nd, we hired a car and drove down toward Hastings
to see our old friend Susan McCrindle. Her husband Ronald was in N. Y. He
was one of the top men in B.O.A.C. for many years.
We loved the drive through
the English country side and Kent is especially beautiful. The McCrindles
have a house built in 1766 with part of an old Moat around it.
Sunday, our old friends from Shanghai, Col. and Mrs. Wilfred Clark,
came up from Farnsborough to have lunch with us and we also had her blind son
Mike Alymer, his wife and little girl.
That morning we walked over to Hyde Park to see the start of the
antique cars racing to Brighton.
There were 250 entries from all over the
world and all cars were made prior to 1905. The drivers and passengers
wore costumes of that time, deer-stalker hats, dusters and the lady's big
hats with veils.
Of course most of them do not finish the 50 mile drive in
the four hours allowed by the rules.
We left London at 10 a.m. on November 5th and again the elapsed
time of the flight was forecast to the minute.
Debby and I had both read
quite a few books about the 400 year search for the N. W. Passage including
a book by Henry Cooper's brother, Paul, which dealt with the disappearance
of Sir John Franklin.
We recognized many of the names of islands, capes
and sounds as we passed over Hudson Bay. It seems hard to believe but we
did the 5,514 miles from London to Los Angeles in just a little bit less
than half a day including a brief refueling stop at Winnepeg.

- 2 -
In Los Angeles we were
met by our old and best Chinese friends
Violet and Ki Chun.
They took us to the Statler Hilton where they had
made reservations for us and that night we had Chinese chow at their son-
in-law "Doc" Wong's restaurant in Chinatown.
We really should
gone because 7 p.m. their time was 3 a.m. for us but we couldn't say "no".
We were with them
almost all the time during the next two days.
We drove
all over Los Angeles and among other things took in the Huntington Library
which neither of us had seen before.
Debby took one morning off to see Jane Gordon.
The evening of Monday the 4th we went to Gordon Chun's home for
drinks followed by Chinese chow at a nearby restaurant.
Florence and "Alli"
Allison, old China hands, were there too and we had a lot of fun.
The next morning, Tuesday, November 5th, the Chuns with their
daughter, Mrs. "Doc" Wong, who was with us practically all the time, despite
three boys and a daughter
to look after at home, called for us at the hotel
and took us to the airport. We took off and climbed up to 35,000 feet.
Our flight forecast was 4:55 (which we hit right on the nose.) I thought
back to the first flight which I made back in 1936 when it took us almost
24 hours to make the run from San Francisco to Honolulu.
When we got on
the ground I also thought back to my first visit here in 1909. As I recall
it we took a two horse-drawn conveyance with three seats to hold the driver
and eight passengers along a dirt road from Honolulu to Waikiki beach.
Today there is just one big apartment building after another all along
beach and back away from it too.
The only thing that hasn't changed is the
weather, the soft gentle air such as exists no where else in the world and
which you can always bank on.
We have decided to leave here on Sunday, November l7th to tly to
Pago Pago in American Samoa from where we will go to British Samoa close
by for a few days and then fly to Fiji which will probably be the best
place to reach us. Address "Care of Pan American World Air Ways, Nandi
Airport, Fiji Islands." An airmail letter (postage 25¢ for each 1/2 oz.)
should reach Nandi from any part of the U.S.A. in about 5 days. We shall
probably not leave Fiji earlier than November 27th.
Last night we had dinner with the Mullaheys at their apartment
at the Diamond Head end of Waikiki beach.
They have a magnificent view
of the whole circular harbor. Dr. and Mrs. Dana Nance and Dr. and Mrs.
Frick Nance were there too.
They are old China hands, members of a
Missionary family born in China.
It was a great pleasure to see them
again. They are both practicing in Honolulu and doing
Debby joins in very best to all,
1 tarael
properties.sfomuseum:description: Typewritten letter from Harold M. Bixby to his family, dated November 13, [1963], in Honolulu; includes description of activities in London, Los Angeles, and Honolulu; reflections on changes over time; mentions Chili [Charles] Vaughn, O.F. Studeman, Jack Kelly, Susan and Ronald McCrindle, Colonel and Mrs. Wilfred Clark, Violet [Violette] and Ki Chun, Gordon Chun, “Alli” [Ernest] and Florence Allison, Dr. and Mrs. Dana Nance, Dr. and Mrs. Frick [Frances] Nance.
